introduction: These hundred readings ask for obedience to the one who speaks for God: observance of his commandments for love of him, acceptance that he does as he wills, and steadfast action on what has been revealed. Their own last pages add that each person must search out truth independently and that conscience is never to be coerced. Passages from other scriptures stand beside them, where the same demand is made in the Torah, the Gospels and the Qur’an, and so do voices that resist it or qualify it: Emerson, Paine and Wollstonecraft on self-trust and blind obedience, Antigone and Socrates on obeying God rather than rulers, Mill on truths that go unquestioned, and the parables of the two sons. They are placed to help a reader ask whom to obey, why, and in what spirit.
questions: The readings join obedience to love: observe My commandments for the love of My beauty. How does obeying someone you love differ from obeying someone you fear?
Emerson and Paine trust only the law within. What in their position do you find true, and what do the readings say that it leaves out?
Antigone, Socrates and the apostles all refuse a human authority in the name of a higher one. How does a person tell a command of God from the command of someone claiming to speak for God?
The elder brother kept every commandment and resented his father's mercy. What does his story say about the spirit in which laws are kept?
The readings close by saying that conscience is never to be coerced and that truth must be explored by each person. How do you hold that together with the call to act precisely as bidden?
Which of the commandments you try to keep has become a delight, and which is still a yoke?

outside.why: In John's Gospel Jesus puts the whole matter in seven words: if ye love me, keep my commandments.
Deuteronomy says that the commandments are given to Israel for its good, to be kept with all the heart and soul.
The psalmist says: O how love I Thy law; it is my meditation all the day.
Proverbs asks a child to let the heart keep the commandments, which add length of days and peace.
Emerson wrote that no law could be sacred to him but that of his own nature. What is lost and what is gained when the only law a person keeps comes from within?
Paul says that every commandment is briefly comprehended in the saying: thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
Rousseau held that the impulse of appetite is slavery, while obedience to a law we prescribe to ourselves is liberty. What changes when a law is chosen and not imposed?
James asks his readers to be doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving their own selves.
Jesus said that not every one who says Lord, Lord shall enter the kingdom, but the one who does the will of the Father.
Jesus said that anyone who will do God's will shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God.
The chief priests asked Jesus in the temple: by what authority doest thou these things, and who gave thee this authority? How is a claim to speak for God to be weighed before it is obeyed?
The Qur’an says of God that He will not be questioned as to what He does, but they will be questioned.
Paul asks in the Letter to the Romans: who art thou, O man, that repliest against God?
Isaiah asks whether the clay shall say to the one who fashions it: what makest thou?
In Isaiah God says: my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways.
The Qur’an says in a single line that whoever obeys the messenger has obeyed God.
Milton's Satan would sooner be free in hell than serve in heaven, and says so with force. Why has his speech moved so many readers, and what answers it?
Jesus said that whoever will be chief among his followers must be their servant.
The people were astonished at Jesus's doctrine, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
God says in the Book of Numbers that with other prophets He speaks in visions and dreams, but with Moses mouth to mouth.
The Qur’an has the believers say: we make no distinction between any of His messengers.
Moses was told that no man can see God's face and live, and was set in a cleft of the rock while the glory passed by.
Asked by Pilate whether he was a king, Jesus answered: my kingdom is not of this world.
Jesus said: my doctrine is not mine, but His that sent me.
Abraham was ready to give up his son at God's command, and was stopped with the words: lay not thine hand upon the lad.
Antigone tells the king that his edict cannot override the unwritten and unfailing statutes of heaven. How is the command of God told apart from the commands of those who hold power?
Jeremiah went down to the potter's house and watched him at work on the wheels, shaping the clay as he chose.

John Stuart Mill argued that even a true opinion, if it is not fully and fearlessly discussed, is held as a dead dogma and not a living truth. Can a teaching be beyond question and still alive in the mind?
Deuteronomy commands: ye shall not add unto the word which I command you.

Shakespeare's Isabella speaks of man, proud man, dressed in a little brief authority and most ignorant of what he is most assured. Why must an authority that none may question belong to no ordinary person?
Jesus said: take my yoke upon you and learn of me, for my yoke is easy and my burden is light.
Isaiah hears God say: behold my servant, whom I uphold; I have put my spirit upon him.
Jeremiah, who pleaded that he was a child, was told: whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak.
Jesus named the first and great commandment: thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, soul and mind.
In the garden Jesus prayed: nevertheless not my will, but Thine, be done.
Ignatius of Loyola prayed: take, Lord, and receive all my liberty, my memory, my intellect and all my will.
In the Qur’an Abraham's son answers: O my father, do that which thou art commanded; thou shalt find me steadfast.
The Qur’an says: O ye who believe, obey God and obey the messenger.
Mary Wollstonecraft wanted minds strengthened so that there would be an end to blind obedience. What distinguishes the obedience these readings ask for from the blind kind?
Jesus said that whoever breaks one of the least commandments and teaches others so shall be called least in the kingdom.
The boy Samuel, called by name in the night, got up and answered: here am I.
Peter and the apostles answered the council: we ought to obey God rather than men.
Thoreau wrote that under a government which imprisons any unjustly, the true place for a just man is also a prison. What does preferring obedience to God cost when other authorities demand otherwise?
Socrates told his judges: I honour and love you, but I shall obey God rather than you.
Jesus likened the one who hears and does his sayings to a wise man who built his house upon a rock.
Leviticus says of the statutes: which if a man do, he shall live in them.
Paul compares the law to the tutors and governors an heir is under until the time appointed by the father. Is obedience a stage to grow out of, or the form that maturity takes?
Jesus said: he that hath my commandments and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me.
In the parable the father sees the son who had left him while he is yet a great way off, and runs to him. How do the readings' hard words about the disobedient sit beside this father?
The first psalm calls blessed the one whose delight is in the law of the Lord.
The Qur’an says: obey God and His messenger, and dispute not one with another lest ye falter.
In the parable the master says: well done, thou good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things.
Exodus promises health to those who diligently hearken to the voice of the Lord and keep His statutes.
The first letter to Timothy says that the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart. If love is what every command is for, how should that shape the way commands are kept?
Samuel told Saul: to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
Thomas Paine declared: my own mind is my own church. What can a single mind not supply for itself?
John Locke argued that the end of law is not to abolish or restrain, but to preserve and enlarge freedom.
The psalmist says: Thy statutes have been my songs in the house of my pilgrimage.
Deuteronomy says that the nations will hear the statutes and say: surely this is a wise and understanding people.
Jesus asked: why call ye me Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?
Jesus rebuked those who tithed mint and cummin and omitted the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy and faith. How is exactness in keeping a law kept from crowding out what the law is for?
The psalmist prays: open Thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of Thy law.
The first letter of John says that this is the love of God, that we keep His commandments, and they are not grievous.
The psalmist says: I will keep Thy law continually, and I will walk at liberty.
James calls blessed the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues in it, not a forgetful hearer but a doer.
Proverbs says that the commandment is a lamp and the law is light.
Naaman went away in a rage at being told only to wash in the Jordan, until his servants came near and reasoned with him.
A soul in Dante's Paradise says of God: His will is our peace.
The elder brother in the parable had never transgressed a commandment, and was angry when his brother was welcomed home. What does obedience without joy show about the one who obeys?
Jesus said: if a man love me, he will keep my words, and my Father will love him, and we will make our abode with him.
The Preacher concludes: fear God, and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of man.
Deuteronomy says that God keeps covenant and mercy with them that love Him and keep His commandments to a thousand generations.
The Qur’an says: there is no compulsion in religion; the right direction is henceforth distinct from error. How can obedience be binding on every soul and yet never be forced?
In the parable of the great supper the invited guests all began to make excuse: a field, five yoke of oxen, a wife.
The Qur’an says: obey God and the messenger when He calls you to that which quickens you.
Isaiah heard the question, who will go for us, and answered: here am I; send me.
Paul says that where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. What kind of liberty lives inside an obedience this complete?
Augustine prayed in the Confessions: give what You command, and command what You will.
Jesus told his disciples to say, when they had done all that was commanded: we are unprofitable servants; we have done our duty.
Emerson's counsel is: trust thyself; every heart vibrates to that iron string. When is following one's own desire self-trust, and when is it what the reading warns against?
The psalmist lifts up his eyes to the hills and says that his help comes from the Lord.
Jesus said that to whom much is given, of him shall much be required.
The first letter of John says that the world passes away, but he that does the will of God abides for ever.
The Qur’an names together the men who obey and the women who obey, and promises them forgiveness and a vast reward.
In Isaiah God says: I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people.
Jesus said to a woman taken in transgression: neither do I condemn thee; go, and sin no more. How do the naming of a wrong and mercy to the wrongdoer go together?
Jesus charged the teachers of his day with laying aside the commandment of God to hold the tradition of men.
Paul asks the Philippians to obey not only in his presence but much more in his absence.
Ezekiel was sent to speak whether his hearers would hear or whether they would forbear.
Jesus said of certain teachers: they be blind leaders of the blind, and both shall fall into the ditch. What makes a learned person an eye to the world and not a blind guide?
Isaiah says that the fast God has chosen is to loose the bands of wickedness and let the oppressed go free. What is an observance such as fasting meant to bring about beyond itself?
The psalmist prays: create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
The Lord's Prayer asks that God's will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
George Herbert wrote that a servant who acts as for God makes drudgery divine.
Paul tells the Galatians that they have been called unto liberty, and asks them by love to serve one another.
Emerson asks each person to watch the gleam of light that flashes across the mind from within.
Mill says that he who knows only his own side of the case knows little of that.
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights says that everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion.
Jefferson's statute for Virginia declares that all men shall be free to profess, and by argument to maintain, their opinions in matters of religion.
Jesus said to Philip: he that hath seen me hath seen the Father.

luke-not-my-will-but-thine.text: Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done
